title: Plasma desktop and widgets respond slowly to images from web browsers being dragged over them, causing rapid drag-and-drop motions to fail
line: Quickly dragging an image from Firefox onto the desktop and dropping it now brings up the drop menu instead of doing nothing.
explanation: Plasma's drop areas (org.kde.draganddrop DropArea, used by the desktop, panels and widgets) wrapped each drag event's data in a MimeData that copied every format up front, and the desktop reads event.mimeData on every drag enter and move. For an image dragged from Firefox that means asking Firefox for the whole image in several formats over the Wayland pipe on each event; Firefox needs more than a second to encode a large image, so Qt waits out its 1 s read timeout per format and plasmashell freezes for 2+ s per event. A drop made during that freeze is never accepted, so it is lost. The event's MimeData now only lists the source's formats and copies a format the first time it is read, so hovering no longer transfers anything and the drop is accepted right away.

commits.message:
draganddrop: read dragged data only when it is needed

Every drag enter and move over a DropArea copied all the dragged data,
so an image dragged from a web browser was transferred again on each
move and a quick drop was lost. The data is now read when it's asked for.

BUG: 505067

media.caption: Pure master: image dragged from Firefox and dropped on the desktop right away; 4 s later nothing has happened
With the fix: the same quick drop brings up the drop menu
Pure master: quick drag and drop of a 33 MB image from Firefox onto the desktop is lost
With the fix: the same quick drop opens the Download / Add Media Frame / Set Image menu

review.text: Clean root-cause fix in kdeclarative's drag-and-drop plugin: DeclarativeMimeData::wrap() lazily wraps the source QMimeData using a QPointer, exposing formats() without transferring payloads during drag enter/move and caching each format in QMimeData on first retrieveData() so QMimeData conversions like urls()/hasUrls() remain identical to the previous full copy. This directly solves the hover freeze and lost rapid drops from browsers across the desktop and all Plasma widgets at the right layer. Before/after media and regression checks match the diff accurately.

reviews.text: Clean root-cause fix in kdeclarative's drag-and-drop plugin: DeclarativeMimeData::wrap() lazily wraps the source QMimeData using a QPointer, exposing formats() without transferring payloads during drag enter/move and caching each format in QMimeData on first retrieveData() so QMimeData conversions like urls()/hasUrls() remain identical to the previous full copy. This directly solves the hover freeze and lost rapid drops from browsers across the desktop and all Plasma widgets at the right layer. Before/after media and regression checks match the diff accurately.

Right layer: kdeclarative's DropArea event eagerly copied every format of the drag (incl. Firefox's large image encodings over the Wayland pipe) on each enter/move; the lazy wrapper defers reads until a format is asked for, which is exactly what the reporter asked for ('slowness should begin when I drop'). Storing each format via QMimeData::setData on first read keeps urls()/hasUrls()/text-uri-list conversion identical to the old copy, and the DeclarativeMimeData lifetime is still bounded by the stack event, so FolderModel/KIO consumers see the same behaviour. Before/after screenshots and strace evidence are convincing; the remaining ~2 s delay after drop (FolderModel copying all formats) is outside the reported hover problem.
